checks.name: calendar-lint
checks.scope: Final10source scoped ESLint, existing intentional full-navigation warning, no suppression or threshold changes.

review.coverage: All6current product files byte-exact through combined immutable reviews: three full new/UI modules, readiness quick form and two additive DTO exact diffs. Nine of ten product/test paths also have exact reviewer hashes; extra existing parent SSR test assertion is a stronger validation-only addition executed by unit suite. Queries/access/token/gate rules unchanged.

findings.area: createWebinarCalendar, date guards (the line checking start/end/now years)
findings.issue: The upper year bound for start and end depends entirely on the imported parseFunnelWebinarSettings. The local guards check only `< 1` for start and end, and check both bounds for `now`. If the parser is later loosened, `utc(start)` or `utc(end)` would emit an extended-year string such as `+010000…`, which is invalid iCalendar.
findings.evidence: The local guard is `start.getUTCFullYear() < 1 || end.getUTCFullYear() < 1 || now.getUTCFullYear() > 9999`. It has no `start/end > 9999` check. The calendar test covers `+010000` only through the parser path, and the parser source is not in the supplied scope.
findings.impact: There is no current exploit, because the parser is said to reject these dates. This is a regression risk: the calendar's own output validity rests on a distant module's contract.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a cheap local assertion that start and end years are between 1 and 9999, or check that `utc(start)` and `utc(end)` match `/^\d{8}T\d{6}Z$/`.
findings.required_test: Keep the `+010000` calendar test. Also add a parser-independent test that the output never contains `+` in a DTSTART or DTEND value.
findings.reason: No present defect: imported canonical parser requires exact four-digit UTC ISO syntax, finite Date.parse and exact canonical ISO equality. Existing negative extended-year/invalid-date tests pass. Loosening that shared contract later is outside this unchanged-parser scope; no duplicate parser or new framework introduced.

findings.issue: No automated test covers the component click path, and the earlier click-path MINOR is still open. Nothing tests the preview no-op, the failure copy when `createWebinarCalendar` returns null, the `.ics` blob download, link cleanup, or revocation of the object URL. The task states that a real browser download has not been verified.
findings.evidence: The supplied tests exercise only `createWebinarCalendar`. The component's `URL.createObjectURL`, `link.click`, `setTimeout` revoke and catch branches have no supplied test.
findings.impact: A regression in the download wiring, the preview guard or the error state would not be caught by the supplied tests.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a jsdom component test with a stubbed `URL.createObjectURL` and `HTMLAnchorElement.click`. Run a browser download smoke test before release.
findings.required_test: Test these cases: (1) a normal click creates a blob with type `text/calendar`, a download name of `webinar.ics`, and a revoke call after 30s using fake timers; (2) preview mode does nothing; (3) an invalid or started event shows the generic alert; (4) a throwing `createObjectURL` shows the download-failure alert.

findings.area: VEVENT property list (UID, DTSTAMP, no SEQUENCE)
findings.issue: A rescheduled event keeps the same UID, and DTSTAMP is the download time. It has no SEQUENCE or LAST-MODIFIED, so some calendar clients may ignore the update or create a duplicate event when a user re-imports a changed schedule.
findings.evidence: The VEVENT lines are UID, DTSTAMP, DTSTART, DTEND, SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION and URL. The test titled 'keeps event identity stable on reschedule' checks only UID and DTSTART/DTEND.
findings.impact: The UI copy already tells users to update their saved event, so the impact is limited to client-specific import behavior.
findings.recommended_fix: Optionally derive a monotonic SEQUENCE from a persisted revision. If none exists, leave this as documented behavior.
findings.required_test: If a revision field is added, test that a changed schedule produces a higher SEQUENCE with the same UID.

findings.area: test "offers the real video library and disables creation with no supported media" (renderToStaticMarkup, `<button[^>]*disabled`)
findings.issue: The no-videos test no longer proves that an empty video list disables creation. Every SSR render now has a disabled submit button because of the hydration guard. The `<button[^>]*disabled` assertion would pass even if `!videos.length` were removed from the button's disabled condition.
findings.evidence: The submit button has `disabled={!hydrated || pending || !videos.length}`. `renderToStaticMarkup` uses the server snapshot, so `hydrated` is false. The assertion therefore matches in both the empty and non-empty cases. The only post-mount test (`createRoot`) uses a non-empty `videos` list and checks only the select.
findings.impact: Removing the empty-library disable condition would not fail any unit test. A merchant with no ready videos could then submit an invalid request after hydration.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a client-mounted test (`createRoot` with `act`) for `videos=[]`. Assert that the submit button is disabled after mount. Add the same test with one video and assert it is enabled.
findings.required_test: After mount, `videos=[]` leaves the submit button disabled and `videos=[one]` leaves it enabled. Also add a `hydrateRoot` test that starts from SSR markup, asserts the controls are disabled before the effects flush, and asserts they are enabled afterwards.

findings.area: fresh-intent block: `completedIntent` read, click "建立另一場", then immediate `inputValue()` comparison
findings.issue: `inputValue()` is read once, not retried, right after a click that starts a full navigation (`window.location.assign`). If the old document is still attached when it runs, it reads the old `requestId`. The `!==` check then fails spuriously.
findings.evidence: `expect((await quick.locator('input[name="requestId"]').inputValue())===completedIntent).toBe(false)` is a one-shot read, not a retrying web-first assertion. Playwright normally waits for navigations the click starts, and the prior diagnostic run got through this step. The risk is a possible timing race rather than an observed failure.
findings.impact: A possible flaky E2E failure that could be misread as an intent-reuse regression.
findings.recommended_fix: Use a retrying assertion, such as `await expect(quick.locator('input[name="requestId"]')).not.toHaveValue(completedIntent)`. Alternatively, wait for the navigation with `page.waitForURL` or `waitForNavigation` before reading the value.
findings.required_test: Run the fresh-intent step repeatedly (for example `--repeat-each=5`). The `requestId` must differ from `completedIntent` every time, with no flakes.
